binders: Arbitrary types Cell, Point, and Parameter.
A normed additive commutative group structure and a real normed-vector-space structure on Parameter.
A grid whose cellRegion maps each cell to a measurable point set and whose constructor data describe a nonempty, pairwise-disjoint cover of its domain.
A Parameter-valued field materialParameters on Point.
hypotheses: Every cell region has measure different from 0.
Every cell region has measure different from ENNReal infinity.
materialParameters is integrable with respect to volumeMeasure restricted to every cell region.
There exist two cells whose computed regional means LocalDef006 are unequal.
conclusions: There exists an assignment from cells to LocalDef001 cell-property wrappers such that, for every cell, the assigned averagedParameter is a valid local average: its region has nonzero finite measure, the field is integrable there, and the value equals the normalized integral over that region.
There exist two cells whose assigned LocalDef001 property wrappers are unequal.
mathematical_definitions: For a region R, measure μ, and field f, LocalDef006(μ,R,f) = (μ(R).toReal)⁻¹ • ∫ f d(μ restricted to R).
LocalDef005(μ,R,f,a) means μ(R) ≠ 0, μ(R) ≠ ∞, f is integrable on R with respect to μ, and a = LocalDef006(μ,R,f).
LocalDef001 packages a Parameter value as a cell property, and LocalDef002 or averagedParameter extracts that value.

The grid's cellRegion projection associates a measurable region to each cell; its constructor additionally records nonemptiness of Cell, pairwise disjointness of unequal-cell regions, and exact coverage of a domain.
translation.proposition_plain_english: For any measurable grid and any integrable real-normed-vector-valued material field, if every cell has positive finite measure and at least two cells have different normalized regional integrals, then one can assign to every cell a property whose averaged parameter is exactly that cell's regional mean, and the resulting assignment takes different property values on at least two cells.

restrictions_and_vacuity_risks: The result is an implication: if no pair of cell averages differs, the heterogeneous-averages antecedent is false and the theorem makes no unconditional heterogeneity claim.
The nonzero, finite-measure, and integrability assumptions are repeated inside LocalDef005; if any fails for a cell, the antecedent is false rather than the conclusion describing a fallback average.
Although the two cells in the unequal-average hypothesis are not explicitly assumed unequal, unequal values force them to be distinct.

A supplied grid carries Nonempty Cell, so the per-cell hypotheses are not vacuous through an empty cell type; universal quantification over a nonexistent grid would nevertheless be vacuous for types admitting no such grid.
The concluding witnesses of unequal assigned properties are existential and are not syntactically required to be the same witnesses as those in the unequal-average hypothesis.

Finiteness and nonzero measure ensure that the ENNReal-to-Real normalization represents a positive finite denominator; the raw definition itself uses toReal and inversion and is total even outside those assumptions.
The conclusion asserts existence, not uniqueness, of the assignment and does not state additional relationships between properties of different cells.

Most grid partition axioms—domain coverage, measurability, and pairwise disjointness—are carried by the grid but are not explicitly used in the displayed logical conditions beyond access to cell regions.
ambiguities: The abstract type Parameter has only real normed-vector-space structure, so no more specific physical interpretation of materialParameters is determined.
The name volumeMeasure is suggestive only; formally it is an arbitrary measure satisfying the stated cellwise assumptions.

The statement compares whole LocalDef001 wrappers in its final clause, while heterogeneity is assumed for their intended averagedParameter values; the inventory presents LocalDef001 as a single-parameter constructor/projection wrapper, so these notions align, but no separate extensionality statement is shown.
The theorem does not specify which unequal cells witness the conclusion, even though the antecedent's witnesses naturally can be reused.
